newsitem.title: CHINA: WEEK AHEAD - Property worries to pressure HK stocks.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - Property worries to pressure HK stocks.

text.p: Hong Kong share prices could come under further selling pressure this week as uncertainty over future government plans to rein in real estate prices hurts property stocks, analysts said.
Hong Kong stocks began a new era under Chinese rule on a shaky note last week, as chief executive Tung Chee-hwa scuppered hopes of a strong market by announcing plans to increase housing supply.

"I don't think there will be strong rebound in the coming week given the situation in the property market. I would not be surprised to see further consolidation in the blue chip index," said Edward Chan, head of research at Amsteel Securities.

The Hang Seng blue chip index tumbled 373.82 points, or 2.46 percent in its first sessions under Chinese rule, ending a holiday-shortened week at 14,822.97 on Friday. The market re-opened on Thursday after a three-day holiday to mark the July 1 handover.
The last remnants of handover euphoria briefly boosted the index to hit an all-time high of 15,363.61 points on Thursday, but property concerns quickly brought investors back down to earth.
"People think that now that the handover is over the good news is in the price," said Ricky Tam, senior research manager at Delta Asia Securities.

With property stocks, which account for about one third of the market capitalisation of the Hang Seng Index, out of favour, analysts said the Hang Seng Index would be unable to make much headway this coming week.
"The market should consolidate or pull back from here," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities.
"There is a lack of buying interest in the property sector. Over the short-term, I don't think the market will have big movement. Just drift down gradually to 14,500 points next week."
As Tung is only expected to reveal the government's property measures in a policy statement in October, uncertainty could weight on the Hang Seng for the next few months, said Chan.
"We don't think that the blue chip index will perform handsomely in the second half of the year," he said.
Miles Remington, sales trader at SocGen-Crosby Securities, said regional re-weightings could see investors move some money out of Hong Kong in the coming week and into other regional markets.
The de facto devaluation of the Thai baht last week had made Thai stocks more attractive, brokers said.
"People will begin to look at regional asset allocations, possibly looking at Singapore and certainly looking at Taiwan," said Remington.
Alex Wong, technical analyst at Dharmala Securities, said if the Hang Seng Index fell below 14,500 points, the market picture could turn quite bearish.
"We will probably see more downside next week but 14,500 should hold," he said, predicting a trading range of 14,600 points to 15,000 points in the coming week.
But Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas, said bargain-hunting could push the index higher this coming week.
"It is likely to go up again and probably break records next week," he said.
